tests.database: vp_mod_workspace on the throwaway Postgres 16; run twice, files in parallel, both green

works: Invite flow end to end: policy approval, one-time link via secret.reveal, only sha256 stored, accept route sets name and password and signs in, expiry, re-invite
Last-owner protection on role change and removal, including two owners demoting each other at the same moment (advisory lock); only an owner can grant or take ownership
API keys: token read once by the approver, only the hash stored, works as Bearer, refused after revoke

Knowledge ingest of text, a generated PDF (pdf-parse, page locations) and a generated DOCX (mammoth, paragraph locations); spans start pending; only approved spans back offering facts; never_say lint; API keys and agents cannot approve spans
Offering and brand edits keep revisions; action.undo restores them and refuses everything else with a reason
Integration credentials staged and stored AES-256-GCM bound to the workspace; never in args, results, lists, activity or action rows
Outbound webhooks signed with the runtime seam sign(); delivered, replayed (approval), retried with backoff, scoped per workspace; private addresses refused
activity.list in plain words with stable pagination and filters; audit chain verifies afterwards
search.global over contacts, agents, campaigns and calls by name or number, wildcards literal
Share links: signed, expiring, revocable, read-only, bound to one object in one workspace
Tenancy: another workspace cannot read or change any of the above (one test touches every tool family)
untested: The tool registry JSON data/workspace-tool-registry.json was not in the repo (also not at research/2026-10-21/blueprint/data/); tool ids and risk classes come from the brief and are my reading of it. Compare my risk classes with the registry when it lands: webhook.replay=external, apikey.revoke=draft, share.link.revoke=draft, knowledge.span.approve=draft, member.remove / integration.disconnect / webhook.delete=destructive
Large or hostile PDFs and DOCX (zip bombs, decompression ratios): only size (9 MB), page (300), passage (600) and 30 s caps; parsing runs in-process
Scanned PDFs (no text) are refused as unreadable; no OCR
Webhook DNS rebinding between the address check and the send; delivery from several server processes at once (claim uses SKIP LOCKED but was run from one)
The 5-second delivery timer inside routes() (switched off under NODE_ENV=test)
Browser or phone use; nothing here has a UI
Share link view of a call includes the transcript: shown only after a policy approval, but there is no redaction step

Uploads over the 9.5 MB route limit (kernel returns 413; the fetch client resets the connection, so it is not asserted); multipart forms are not parsed (send the file as the body, or JSON). Cookie sessions must still send JSON (kernel CSRF rule), so raw uploads need an API key
needs_from_others: Kernel owner: Registry.approve() stores args and result in clear in action.args / action.result and GET /v1/actions returns them. Workspace works around it (secret.reveal, integration.stage_secrets); a redaction hook would let other modules hold secrets safely. Logged as risk.2026-10-21.kernel-stores-approval-args-and-results-in-clear in the inbox

Deployment: set VP_SECRET_KEY (32 bytes as 64 hex characters or base64). Without it integration.connect, webhook.create, secret holds and share links fail with a clear error. Never set VP_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE or VP_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_HTTP in production

Other modules: announce events by calling the webhook.emit tool with a system actor (registry.execute(pool, "webhook.emit", {event, data}, {workspaceId, actor: {type: "system"}})); server code that needs an integration credential can import integrationSecrets from the workspace module
